hints: Look at the carbon that carries the Br atom and ask how many other carbons it is directly joined to, that tells you the classification.
Expand the condensed formula to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CBr}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and find the longest continuous carbon chain.
Number that longest chain from the end that gives the Br and the methyl branch the lowest numbers, then combine the two parts of the answer.
walkthrough:
**Expand the structure and find the parent chain**

First, let's write it out in full so you can see it clearly. It is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{Br})(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

Count the longest chain through the C-Br carbon: 3 carbons to the left + 1 central + 2 to the right = 6 carbons, plus one methyl branch. So the parent is hexane.

**Name it by numbering for lowest locants**

Now number to give substituents the smallest numbers. From the right, the C-Br carbon is carbon 3. From the left, it would be carbon 4.

So we choose numbering from the right:
$$\text{C1 - C2 - C3(Br)(CH}_3\text{) - C4 - C5 - C6}$$
This gives 3-bromo-3-methylhexane.

**Classify as primary, secondary or tertiary**

Classification depends only on the carbon bonded to the halogen. Count how many other carbons that C-Br carbon is joined to.

It is joined to $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, to $\text{CH}_3$, and to $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. That is three alkyl groups, so it is tertiary.

options.A: The name 3-bromo-3-methylhexane is correct, but secondary is wrong. Secondary means the C-Br carbon is joined to only two other carbons. Here it is joined to three carbons, so it is tertiary.
options.B: This is correct on both parts. Numbering from the right gives the lowest locants, 3-bromo-3-methylhexane, and the C-Br carbon is bonded to three other carbons, so it is a tertiary halogenoalkane.
options.C: Tertiary is correct, but 3-bromo-4-methylhexane is wrong. Both the Br and the methyl are on the same carbon (carbon 3 when numbered correctly). Splitting them to 3 and 4 comes from inconsistent or incorrect numbering.
options.D: Both parts are wrong. 4-bromo-5-methylhexane comes from numbering from the wrong end, which gives higher locants than 3,3. It is also not secondary because the C-Br carbon has three C-C bonds, not two.
